cells.tense: Right now something is arriving clean and nothing has been asked of it yet.
cells.ask: Follow one thing that's genuinely caught your eye today and tell someone about it. No shaping it into a lesson first.
cells.core:
Something's catching your eye before you've decided whether to look. That's the new part. Not the insight you'd frame on a slide, not the polished version you'd pitch — the flash before the polish, working the way it should.

That nothing has been cut yet is not fault. It means you are early and free. You get to say what this is before it has to mean something. Balance here is that freedom held open. What it's free to feed next is depth — let what's caught you be caught in front of someone else, without first dressing it up.

The uncut beginning is yours on loan, and the loan wants feeding. Follow the one thing, tell one person, as it came.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead is the moment all this noticing finally pays off and you're already there, waiting.
cells.ask: Open one thing you care about — a book, a room, a problem — with no angle on it. Look thirty seconds and leave it as found.
cells.core:
You're living at the finish line of an insight that hasn't unfolded yet. Everything that catches you gets auditioned for what it could become — the point, the pitch, the payoff — and it's all happening in service of a future that can't be guaranteed. Notice the pressure: the flicker arrives and immediately has a job.

What that costs is the openness that made the flicker worth anything. Wanting to prove you have it is doing the steering now, and it's hurrying the thing this openness was for.

Put it down for a while. Not forever — long enough to meet something without knowing what it means. The planning will still be there when you come back.

cells.tense: The pull that once set your direction is behind you now and you're still standing at a door already closed.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're good at and do it once today on purpose, with the choice made from where you are now.
cells.core:
Looking up and finding your own direction isn't happening. What's there instead is drift. You can still move through the day, but nothing is yours to steer toward by choice. On the good days it runs the other way: something catches you, you know which way to turn, and the turning is easy — not because the pull is louder, but because the choice is yours.

Pushing yourself to feel pulled won't bring it back. What restores the steering is doing one thing on purpose — something you're good at — and letting the direction come from the doing rather than from the feeling. Energy goes into the action, and the action pulls the orientation back through.

The bearing doesn't return because you search. It returns while you're walking.

cells.tense: You're catching what's arriving right now and filing it under somebody else's name.
cells.ask: When something next catches you, say out loud 'I'm the one noticing this' — once, before you move on.
cells.core:
You catch what's coming — first in the room to register the shift, often before there's a name for it. You describe that as staying ahead, or being sensitive, or reading the room. The astuteness is real and running now. What hasn't caught up is the credit.

It isn't something you'll start doing later. It's already happening and getting filed under other people's names — the group's, the moment's, your discipline's. None of those hand the credit back to you.

Bring it down one level: not the system you've built around catching things, just the plainest form. When the next flicker lands, mark that it landed through you.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is in the Too Little cell — that the person stopped being present to a pull that once registered. The record gives only the 'Restored' face of the card, not the history, so the cell points at the absence of present steering without naming what happened there or what it cost. A reader could reasonably say the pull is still there and simply being questioned, not dropped; the read still lands because the ask stands on its own. The sentence that serves me more than the person would be any line that locates a source for the disappearance, and it has been kept out.
